title: Adaptive Classical-Query Bound for FX
summary: For FX, the bound is established and matched by a non-adaptive attack for non-adaptive classical queries; whether it extends to adaptive queries remains unproved.

formal_statement.body: For the FX construction, given $D$ non-adaptive classical chosen-plaintext queries, a quantum adversary requires at least $2^{n+\kappa}/D$ quantum queries to the underlying cipher $E$ to recover the key, and a matching attack is also non-adaptive. The unresolved question is whether the same quantum query lower bound, $2^{n+\kappa}/D$, remains valid when the classical chosen-plaintext queries are adaptive, for an $n$-bit block size and a $\kappa$-bit key.

scope.domain: Quantum query complexity for key recovery in symmetric cryptanalysis of the FX construction.
parameters: D, the number of classical chosen-plaintext queries
n, the block size in bits
kappa, the key size in bits
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the same quantum-query lower bound remains valid when the classical chosen-plaintext queries are adaptive.

citations.label: Beyond quadratic speedups in quantum attacks on symmetric schemes

progress.summary: The source presents a lower bound and matching non-adaptive attack for non-adaptive classical chosen-plaintext queries. It identifies extending the same bound to adaptive classical queries as likely but not formally proven.
citation_labels: Xavier Bonnetain et al., Beyond quadratic speedups in quantum attacks on symmetric schemes
